name: East Coast
summary: Park connector living, sea breeze, and a slower weekend tempo east of town — still the default family shortlist for many Western packages.
body: East Coast (Marine Parade, Siglap, Frankel, parts of Katong adjacency) rewards people who want outdoor space and a neighbourhood feel without going full heartland. East Coast Park is the weekend engine — cycling, hawker breakfasts, beach sports, kite season drama, and the daily dog-walk grid for pet households who cannot put animals on the MRT. Commutes into CBD are longer than Holland V or River Valley, but the East Coast Line (Marine Parade, Marine Terrace, Siglap) changed the calculus for non-drivers. Housing spans park-facing condos, older walk-ups, landed streets inland, and HDB-adjacent pockets for eligible tenants. Condo visitor parking and pet by-laws vary estate-to-estate — ask the guardhouse and get pet clauses in the TA before you ship crates. School gravity is real: UWCSEA East and several other campuses pull families into this belt, which supports rents even when CBD workers complain about the ride. Compare honestly with Tampines if you want more internal space per dollar, or Katong/Joo Chiat if you want denser F&B walkability. Grocery ops split cleanly: wet-market / neighbourhood FairPrice for greens, RedMart for heavy pantry water runs.
watchOuts: Longer CBD commute than central belts
Car still helps for off-corridor errands and pet taxis
Condo visitor parking / pet by-laws vary
housingMix: Condos facing the park, landed inland, some HDB for eligible renters.
commuteNotes: East Coast Line (Marine Parade, Marine Terrace, Siglap); expressways to CBD; buses along East Coast Road.
